history_policy: This version hash-inherits every V21 scored workload, mode, job count, checksum, timing boundary, engine-availability ruling, acceptance decision, attribution metric, external-suite boundary, lifecycle profile, no-JIT profile, exact-parent metric, collection guard, and publication boundary. It changes no scored row or production engine behavior. It re-pins only the exact-parent integration after that collector admitted the already-frozen single_no_jit runner mode. Any later workload, boundary, jobs, checksum, metric source, adapter, integration ruling, or acceptance change creates another version.
change: Re-freezes the completed exact-parent integration after its runner-argument contract admitted the existing single_no_jit mode. The collector's identities, evidence schema, metrics, alternating order, quality guards, publication policy, and every scored workload remain inherited unchanged.

contract_changes: frontend compiler counters are retained with every sample
competing long-running jobs reject collection before sampling
transient overlap rejects the affected exact pair
structural self-test JSON fixtures are cloned without a host convenience global
context_lifecycle samples preserve and validate their frozen auxiliary telemetry row
single_no_jit samples preserve the frozen required-bytecode mode identity
exact_parent_integration.publication_boundary: Only an explicitly selected quiet-reference host on AC power may support an efficiency or lifecycle claim. Required counters must be measured and stable at at most 5% RSD, every thermal observation must remain nominal, generated-code/cache claims additionally require their exact category metric, and every raw sample remains visible. Context lifecycle collection additionally requires the frozen options/checksum profile, exact phase and finalizer reconciliation, and bounded post-destroy RSS checkpoints. Required-bytecode/no-JIT collection additionally preserves the frozen single_no_jit mode and workload checksum. Diagnostic hosts never gate or support a public ratio.
